the role of histone acetylation in the pathogenesis of alcohol‐induced liver disease.
the role of histone modifications in acetaldehyde exposure‐induced genomic instability.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
acetaldehyde exposure leads to the formation of acetylated histones, which in turn affects chromatin accessibility and chromatin structure, and ultimately impacts gene expression.

acetaldehyde exposure causes a significant decrease in histone H4 and histone H3 acetylation, and a significant decrease in nucleosome levels in the chromatin of BEAS‐2b cells, which may contribute to the increase in general DNA accessibility and the decrease of nucleosome occupancy at the genomic loci in acetaldehyde treated cells.
acetaldehyde can induce a wide range of histone modifications, including histone acetylation, methylation and ubiquitination, and chromatin remodeling in human bronchus epithelial BEAS-2B cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
acetaldehyde exposure can affect histone modifications, chromatin assembly, and chromatin structure and that these effects may contribute to acetaldehyde‐associated pathogenesis.
